member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.External.AdjustedRandIndex
member.summary: Adjusted Rand Index (ARI): the Rand Index corrected for chance agreement. ARI = (RI − E[RI]) / (max(RI) − E[RI]) computed via the contingency-table identity ARI = (sum_index − expected) / (max_index − expected) where sum_index = Σ C(n_ij, 2), expected = sum_a · sum_b / C(n, 2), max_index = (sum_a + sum_b) / 2.

remarks.para: Why ARI over raw Rand. The raw Rand Index is biased upward — random partitions of similar size achieve high scores by accident. ARI subtracts the expected value under a permutation null model so a score of 0 genuinely means "no better than chance," which makes scores comparable across datasets of different sizes and class counts.
Symmetry. Symmetric in its two arguments.
Edge cases. Returns 1.0 when both inputs are identical-partition (or trivially when both have a single cluster and N ≤ 1). Returns 0.0 when both are empty.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.External.Completeness
member.summary: Completeness: a partition is complete if all observations from a reference class are grouped into a single predicted cluster. c = 1 − H(predicted | reference) / H(predicted)

remarks.para: Range. [0, 1]; 1.0 means every reference class is fully contained in a single predicted cluster. Higher is better.

Asymmetric. Like , this is directional. Completeness asks "do my clusters preserve class togetherness?" — the dual question to homogeneity's "do my clusters preserve class identity?". combines the two as a harmonic mean.
Symmetry with Homogeneity. Completeness(pred, truth) == Homogeneity(truth, pred).
Edge cases. Returns 1.0 when the predicted partition is trivial (single cluster — every reference class is trivially fully contained). Returns 0.0 for empty input.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.External.ContingencyTable
member.summary: Internal helper that builds a contingency table from two parallel label arrays. The shape every entropy-based external index (NMI, ARI, Homogeneity, Completeness, V-measure) starts from — densify both label sets once and tally pairwise co-occurrences.

remarks.para: Output. A dense int[rows, cols] matrix where rows is the predicted-class count and cols is the reference-class count. counts[r, c] is the number of observations whose predicted label maps to index r and whose reference label maps to index c. The dense densified spaces are also returned via out parameters so callers can use them for marginal calculations without re-densifying.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.External.Homogeneity
member.summary: Homogeneity: a partition is homogeneous if each predicted cluster contains observations from only a single reference class. h = 1 − H(reference | predicted) / H(reference)

remarks.para: Range. [0, 1]; 1.0 means every predicted cluster is purely from one reference class. Higher is better.

Asymmetric. Homogeneity is not symmetric: h(pred, truth) ≠ h(truth, pred). It measures one direction — "do my clusters preserve class identity?" Pair with ("are class members kept together?") for the symmetric pair, and for the harmonic mean.
Edge cases. Returns 1.0 when the reference partition is trivial (single class — perfectly homogeneous by definition). Returns 0.0 for empty input.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.External.IExternalClusterEvaluator
member.summary: External cluster validation index. Measures agreement between a predicted partition and a reference labeling (typically a ground truth, but any reference partition works).

remarks.para: Input contract. Both label arrays must have equal length; labels need not be densely-numbered. Implementations densify internally as needed.
Family. External indices (Purity, Normalized Mutual Information, Adjusted Rand Index, V-measure, Fowlkes-Mallows) live here. Indices that measure quality without a reference live in .
Symmetry. External indices are not in general symmetric in their two arguments (Purity definitely isn't; NMI and ARI are). Concrete implementations document which argument plays which role.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.External.NormalizedMutualInformation
member.summary: Normalized Mutual Information (NMI), arithmetic-mean normalization: NMI = 2·I(U;V) / (H(U) + H(V)) where I is mutual information and H is Shannon entropy of the marginal cluster distributions. Range [0, 1]; 1.0 indicates perfect agreement (up to relabeling).

remarks.para: Normalization choice. Several variants exist (arithmetic mean, geometric mean sqrt(H(U)·H(V)), maximum). The arithmetic mean form is what scikit-learn returns as normalized_mutual_info_score and is the most commonly cited "NMI" in clustering literature; this evaluator returns that form.
Symmetry. Symmetric in the two arguments — swapping predicted and reference labels gives the same value.
Edge cases. Returns 1.0 when both partitions are trivial (single cluster — both entropies zero, undefined ratio resolved to perfect-agreement by convention). Returns 0.0 for empty input.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.External.Purity
member.summary: Purity: (1/N) · Σ_p max_r |p ∩ r| — the fraction of observations whose predicted cluster is dominated by their reference class. Range [0, 1]; 1.0 indicates perfect agreement.

remarks.para: Reading. Purity rewards predicted clusters that contain a single reference class but does not penalize over-fragmentation — the trivial partition "every observation in its own cluster" achieves purity 1.0 by construction. Read alongside the predicted cluster count, or paired with a complementary index like NMI/ARI that penalizes fragmentation, to detect this failure mode.

Asymmetry. Purity is not symmetric in its arguments: Purity(pred, truth) ≠ Purity(truth, pred) in general. The canonical convention — and the one used here — is to take the max over reference classes within each predicted cluster.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.External.VMeasure
member.summary: V-measure: harmonic mean of and . V = 2·h·c / (h + c)

remarks.para: Range. [0, 1]; 1.0 requires both perfect homogeneity and perfect completeness simultaneously. Higher is better.
Symmetric. Unlike its two constituents, V-measure is symmetric in its arguments — homogeneity and completeness swap under argument swap, and the harmonic mean is invariant to that swap.

When to prefer V-measure. Use this when you want a single scalar that punishes both over-clustering (low homogeneity) and under-clustering (low completeness). For asymmetric questions — "does my clustering preserve class identity but it's OK if it splits classes across clusters" — use alone.
Edge cases. Returns 0.0 when either component is 0 (the harmonic mean of 0 and anything is 0). Returns 0.0 for empty input.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.Internal.CalinskiHarabaszEvaluator
member.summary: Calinski-Harabasz index: ratio of between-cluster scatter to within-cluster scatter, F-statistic-flavored: (BSS / (K−1)) / (WSS / (N−K)). Higher is better.

remarks.para: Edge cases. Returns when the index is undefined (fewer than 2 clusters, or N ≤ K). Returns when within-cluster scatter is zero (a degenerate but mathematically clean limit).
Distance metric. Hardcoded to Euclidean — same caveat as .

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.Internal.DaviesBouldinEvaluator
member.summary: Davies-Bouldin index: average over clusters of the worst-case (scatter_i + scatter_j) / separation_{ij} ratio. Lower is better; 0 indicates perfectly compact, well-separated clusters.

remarks.para: Edge cases. Returns when there are fewer than 2 clusters (DB index is undefined). Returns when any two cluster centroids coincide (separation 0).
Distance metric. Hardcoded to Euclidean — same caveat as .

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.Internal.IInternalClusterEvaluator
member.summary: Internal cluster validation index. Measures partition quality using only the data and the partition itself — no ground truth required.

remarks.para: Input contract. data is row-major (one observation per row, equal-length rows); labels is parallel to data, one cluster label per observation. Labels need not be densely-numbered; implementations densify internally.

Family. Internal indices (Silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, Calinski-Harabasz) live here. Indices that compare two label arrays (Purity, NMI, ARI) live in ; domain-specific indices that consume additional structure (e.g. graph + edge observables) live in their owning domain assembly (Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Evaluators, etc.).
Score direction. Higher-or-lower-is-better is index-specific; each concrete implementation documents its direction.

member.name: T:Clustering.Evaluation.Internal.SilhouetteEvaluator
member.summary: Silhouette coefficient: s_i = (b_i − a_i) / max(a_i, b_i) averaged over points, where a_i is the mean intra-cluster distance and b_i is the mean distance to the nearest other cluster. Range [−1, 1]; higher is better.

remarks.para: Edge cases. Singletons score 0 (no intra-cluster pair to average over). Partitions with fewer than 2 clusters return 0.0 (silhouette is undefined).
Distance metric. Currently hardcoded to Euclidean. A future revision should accept an injectable IDistanceMetric so non-Euclidean data (Mahalanobis, product manifolds, etc.) can be scored honestly.
